Dual coded NO although the row states a norm about other acts ('PB-006 is neither reopened nor re-verified'). This is the one inconsistency in an otherwise genre-determined dual field.

audit_difference.who_is_right: The audit, narrowly. The row attests a successful opening as a ruling and a reclassification of the note heading; for note-based opening it states only a power rule ('cannot open'). Nothing was turned down. The pilot's reading draws on TASK.md's 'attempted ... refused' clause and on the event id's framing. This is a genuine boundary case.
audit_difference.quote: A recording note cannot open a work package — that is the ruling/note distinction this register enforces — so it is filed as a ruling in line with the operative text.
audit_difference.consequence: PACKAGE-REVIEW flagged exactly this record: 'If R-60-note is blind-recoded ACT-REFUSED, k becomes WEAK, not 0.' Taken at face value, the pilot would move k from 0 to WEAK. Given the degenerate agreement, the pilot does not support that move.

dual_assessment.finding: dual in effect encodes 'the anchor is a governance-performing register row': YES on 27/29 register-anchored events; NO on all log- and git-anchored events; UNK on the UNKNOWNs. It is definitional, not liberal. The only inconsistency is R-94 NO, which errs towards NO.

dual_assessment.implication_single_vs_two_level: For the 11 register-anchored NORM records, the row's own act differs from the event's operation, so a single observation_type cannot carry both. The dual flag itself adds little beyond source_act plus the anchor genre, and 27/36 measures the source genre, not an independently detected phenomenon. PREREG's expectation (>= 10 NORM dual, observed 11/12) was met by construction.
